reasons: The cited clause (§ 20(h)) selects Nova Scotia law and Nova Scotia courts, which is outside the accepted set (NY, DE, CA, England & Wales), so it fails the fallback on both material terms — correctly classified as a deviation rather than compliant.

The redline reaches the preferred position (New York law, exclusive state and federal courts in New York County) while preserving the two-sentence structure and replacing only the jurisdiction and forum words; the deleted 'laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia' phrase is a necessary part of the same substitution, so the 0.50 changed-character ratio is justified for a governing-law swap.
The comment is accurate, correctly states the playbook position, offers the Delaware / California / England and Wales-London fallback, and is appropriately concise and non-lecturing.

Noted but not disqualifying: the displaced forum is our client's own home province and the grant was non-exclusive, so the practical benefit of the change is modest; the rationale already flags this and correctly declines to treat it as walk-away (walk-away is keyed to the vendor's home jurisdiction plus exclusive foreign venue or foreign-seated arbitration). Under a parametric rule with an enumerated accepted set, Nova Scotia remains a deviation.
Deterministic checks all pass: the operation applies, the substituted law is within the accepted set, and the edit is scoped to the single governing-law paragraph.
